domain: Political Linguistics / State Formation / Cultural Engineering
topic_summary: Analysis of Turkey's 1928 alphabet reform (Law 1353), which replaced the Ottoman Arabic script with a Latin-based alphabet within three months. The reform represents an extreme case of top-down linguistic engineering with effectively zero prior practitioners of the new script, creating a generational literacy rupture while serving Atatürk's modernization project.

key_entities: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk (reform architect; authoritarian modernizer)
Language Commission / Dil Encümeni (technical implementers; linguists and educators)
Ottoman literate class (8-10% of population; Arabic-script readers rendered functionally illiterate)
Nation's Schools / Millet Mektepleri (compulsory re-education infrastructure)
Traditionalist opposition (Kâzım Karabekir; Islamic unity advocates)
key_tensions: Three-month implementation vs. five-year transition proposal (Atatürk vs. Language Commission)
Modernization imperative vs. Ottoman cultural continuity (state vs. traditionalists)
Legal prohibition vs. persistent Ottoman script use (formal law vs. social practice)
Generational literacy rupture (post-1928 cohort vs. pre-1928 literate class)
Phonetic adequacy claim vs. cultural severance cost (technical justification vs. heritage access)
Democratic rhetoric vs. authoritarian implementation (Atatürk's stated ideals vs. coercive enforcement)

omegas.description: KERNEL COLLAPSE: This is NOT a contested kernel. There was no prior occupancy of the Latin-script reading to contest. The 'kernel' (writing system choice) had only one socially instantiated reading (Ottoman Arabic script) before 1928. The reform installed a NEW kernel with zero prior practitioners, not a new reading of an existing contested kernel. The absence of M-set (practitioners of the new reading) is the structural fact, not evidence of kernel contestation. What appears contested is the LEGITIMACY of kernel replacement (modernization vs. tradition), not competing readings of a shared commitment. Reclassified as standard constraint decomposition.

Is script_phonetic_adequacy a true Mountain (linguistic physics) or a Tangled_Rope (technical justification serving political project)? The Arabic abjad's vowel inadequacy for Turkish is measurable, but the NECESSITY of alphabet replacement (vs. diacritic reform) is contested. Ottoman script had been used for 600 years; sudden inadequacy claim may be post-hoc rationalization. Preliminary classification as Mountain may collapse to Rope upon generation.
omegas.source: F03 (Hasty Generalization) + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: Deferred axis ottoman_script_persistence suggests Law 1353's formal prohibition did not achieve complete social compliance. Oral histories and archival evidence show continued informal use. The gap between legal kernel installation and social embedding may be larger than the 'three-month success' narrative suggests. High-epsilon deferred axis warranting future investigation.
omegas.source: Deferred axis ottoman_script_persistence + research context on persistence

omegas.description: The 8-10% pre-reform literacy rate is cited as evidence of Arabic script inadequacy, but causation is unclear. Was low literacy due to script phonetic mismatch, or due to Ottoman educational infrastructure limits? Post-reform literacy gains may reflect Nation's Schools expansion rather than script superiority. Confounding variable not disentangled in available research.

Research notes Law 1353 has been used to prosecute Kurds for using non-Turkish alphabet letters. This suggests the reform's extractiveness extends beyond generational literacy rupture to ethnic-linguistic suppression. Victim set may be broader than modeled. Potential additional axis (linguistic_minority_suppression) not developed due to limited research context.
omegas.source: Research context on enforcement + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: script_phonetic_adequacy classified as Mountain but the necessity of full alphabet replacement (vs. diacritic reform of Arabic script) is contested. The 600-year use of Ottoman script suggests adequacy is relative to educational infrastructure, not absolute linguistic physics. Generated omega_mountain_validity to bound this uncertainty. Additionally, the user's kernel contest framing was rejected: this is NOT a contested kernel (no prior readings to contest), but rather a case of authoritarian kernel REPLACEMENT with zero M-set. Generated omega_not_contested_kernel to document the reclassification.
